title: Hinoki Steam
premise: A decades-spanning drama at a mountain hot-spring inn. Xiaoyou and Ali are easily confused; the hinoki bath tub goes intact→cracked→hoop-repaired; the guest carriage is wrecked and must be avoided; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_keeper: Hot-spring innkeeper Afu around fifty, salt-and-pepper short beard, deep-blue yukata under a short jacket, copper key ring at the waist, warm solid smile.
states.scalded_with_cane: The same keeper after a scald: right calf bandage seeping, limping on a bamboo cane, short-jacket cuff scorched.
states.deceased: Afu has closed his eyes in death, lying still on the corridor tatami, face peaceful, no breath left.

states.young_apprentice: Young Xiaoyou: a lean girl attendant of fourteen or fifteen, vermilion hair ribbon, pale-cyan yukata, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult_successor: Adult Xiaoyou: a steady young woman keeper in her twenties, still in vermilion hair ribbon, yukata swapped for a deep-blue short jacket.

states.intact: A man-tall round hinoki bath tub, fine wood grain, brass hoops, inn family crest carved on the rim.
states.cracked_leaking: The same hinoki bath tub with a crack in the wall, brass hoop loose, hot water seeping along the seam.
states.hoop_repaired: The tub crack packed with new wood wedges, brass hoop retightened, crest still there, ready to hold water again.

states.intact: A lacquer-black guest-account water board with neat white chalk writing, hung on the office wall.
states.steam_blurred: The same water board blurred by hot-spring steam, writing bled, lacquer blistered.

states.intact: A deep-red two-wheel carriage, striped cushions in the cabin, inn family crest painted on the door, a gentle shaft horse.
states.overturned_wrecked: The deep-red carriage overturned into a creek ditch, shafts snapped, cushions soaked—a wreck that can no longer be driven.

states.young_rival: Ali, nearly identical in face to young Xiaoyou, dark-green hair ribbon, bold expression, a yew wood hairpin under the ear.
states.adult_rival: Adult Ali still in dark-green hair ribbon and yew wood hairpin under the ear, expression deeper.

segments.action: At dusk, Afu steps across wet blue stone into the open-air bath and tests the water.
A row of five washi lanterns hangs on the bath stone lamp posts; Afu lights them one by one.
Under the office corridor eaves hang two bath-opening brass bells; Afu reaches out and lets them ring softly.
Afu checks whether the brass hoops of the hinoki bath tub have loosened.
Through the bath steam, Afu looks toward the cedar-forest night lamps.
The hinoki bath tub fills with spring water; the wood grain shines in the lantern light.
Afu sits on the blue-stone rim and listens to the creek.
In the office corridor Afu opens a chalk box and writes room numbers on the guest-account water board.
Afu sketches tonight's bath open hours in a blank corner of the water board.
Afu claps chalk dust from his hands and steps back to study the water board.
A paper lantern in the corridor sways; wood-grain gleam from the hinoki bath tub sweeps Afu's profile.
In the morning office corridor, Afu greets young Xiaoyou driving the guest carriage in.
Xiaoyou stops the deep-red carriage by the corridor stone steps and straightens the striped cushions.
Afu points to three yukata wood clips on the bamboo pole, teaching Xiaoyou to read color dots and room types.
Xiaoyou crouches in the corridor, curiously touching the tatami edge.
Afu explains to Xiaoyou the signals for opening and closing the bath.
Xiaoyou looks back at the intact guest carriage, eyes full of longing.
Behind a noren on the mountain-gate town street, Ali in a dark-green hair ribbon turns to look.

segments.action: The hinoki bath tub quietly steams in the night mist.
In snow season, day after day Afu sweeps the bath blue stone.
Another rainy night, Afu checks the tub's brass hoops.
In peach-blossom season, Afu watches returning guests' lamps through the steam.
At midsummer noon, Afu wipes stone lamp posts heated by the sun.
Autumn leaves cover the corridor; Afu keeps watch alone until dawn.
At dawn, Afu patrols the office corridor; the guest carriage waits by the stone steps.
Afu crouches to check the carriage shaft joints.
Afu walks to the bamboo pole; those three yukata wood clips still hang in place.
A strange blue-canopy carriage passes the mountain road—narrower cabin, not the deep-red guest carriage.
Afu stands on the stone steps, logging last night's spring-temperature swings.
Afu hangs yukata on the corridor bamboo pole.
At midnight spring pressure spikes; the open-air bath boils; the hinoki bath tub shakes hard.
Hot steam swallows the stone lamp posts; lantern paper wrinkles.
A sharp crack—the hinoki bath tub wall bursts, brass hoop loose and leaking.

segments.action: A black-hood rented rickshaw stops in the corridor, nothing like the long-wrecked guest carriage.
The hot-spring guild chief steps down and talks beside Afu; the two are similar in build.
The guild chief points at the rickshaw, explaining temporary guest pickup.
The rickshaw leaves; Afu alone in the corridor watches it go.
On the mountain-gate town street comes a yuzu-candy girl in a light-brown hair ribbon; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Xiaoyou.
The girl practices handing candy; Afu shakes his head—she is not Xiaoyou after all.
Years later at dusk, Afu with a seeping bandage on his right calf leans on a bamboo cane before the abandoned bathhouse.
